title_candidates: The Lighthouse Radio Operator vs. the Giant Crab — Full Survival Movie
She Survived the Crash — Then the Creature Led Her Back
Nobody Believed the Small Animal Mattered — Until It Saved Them All
logline: After a violent wreck in a tidal lighthouse station cut off after a supply ferry wrecks on black rock flats, Noor must use lighthouse radio operator knowledge, bent brass foghorn valve key, and trust in vulnerable creatures to rescue survivors from a barnacle-armored giant crab that hunts through tidal channels.
audience_promise: A compressed visual-first creature-survival film: immediate disaster, giant predator readability, innocent animal stakes, morally differentiated creatures, occupational problem-solving, quiet care, trap preparation, rescue closure, and minimal dialogue.

survival_engine.vehicle_or_station: the stranded ferry hull and the lighthouse foghorn/lens mechanism
survival_engine.predator: a barnacle-armored giant crab that hunts through tidal channels
survival_engine.innocent_animal: an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire
survival_engine.ally_creature: an ancient leatherback turtle carrying moss and shell scars
survival_engine.rescue_inversion: escape becomes rescue when captives and the allied creature are found alive but trapped

emotional_engine.wound: Noor believes the wreck proves she failed the people and animals under her care.
emotional_engine.want: survive the predator territory and reach safety
emotional_engine.need: accept that care, humility, and reciprocal rescue matter more than escaping alone or proving invulnerability
emotional_engine.injustice: the disaster is not a human villain's plot; the cruelty is exposure, predation, injury, and the temptation to abandon weaker lives
emotional_engine.protective_counterforce: an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire and an ancient leatherback turtle carrying moss and shell scars create trust through vulnerability rather than speech
emotional_engine.belonging_payoff: the wrecked space becomes the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home; the turtle returns to open water with the seabird chick safe on its mossy shell
emotional_engine.secret_or_power_asymmetry: the predator owns the terrain while the protagonist owns only professional knowledge, tools, and attention to vulnerable life
emotional_engine.cost_of_failure: survivors remain trapped, the innocent animal is abandoned, the creature ally is captured, and the protagonist escapes with guilt instead of home

protagonist.identity: Noor, a lighthouse radio operator who knows the foghorn, lens room, tide charts, and ferry emergency panels
protagonist.vulnerability: injury, isolation, guilt, limited weapons, and dependence on terrain she cannot control
protagonist.capability: lighthouse radio operator competence, mechanical improvisation, observation of animal behavior, and refusal to abandon weaker lives
protagonist.agency_first_action: she protects or frees an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire before understanding how it can help her
protagonist.transformation: from guilty survivor to rescue author who reads the ecosystem instead of dominating it

opening_event.first_10_seconds: Noor is knocked against the radio desk as the ferry breaks apart outside the lighthouse
opening_event.first_60_seconds: the disaster becomes physically undeniable; the first injury, animal distress, or survivor separation is visible before any explanation.
opening_event.first_5_minutes: a barnacle-armored giant crab that hunts through tidal channels appears in scale relation to the protagonist; an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire and the first sign of an ancient leatherback turtle carrying moss and shell scars establish that the ecosystem is morally differentiated.
opening_event.dramatic_question: can she turn professional knowledge and care for vulnerable creatures into rescue before the predator owns the terrain?

theme_lane.family_or_heir_hook: innocent animal protection and reciprocal creature rescue
theme_lane.romance_hook: the ferry mate who dismissed the seabird as a nuisance helps carry it to the turtle before apologizing
theme_lane.modern_power_hook: occupational competence, disaster machinery, visual survival problem-solving, and creature ecology

nearest_failures: escape-only ending that abandons the animal/creature relationship
professional identity used as costume rather than survival mechanism
continuous noise/action with no quiet care hinge
mitigations: pay the role/creature/location contract within two minutes
keep every objective legible with sound off
make the opening vehicle or station become the final trap/rescue machine
use silence, breath, creature texture, and small animal contact after the first pursuit
reveal captives or the allied creature in danger so escape becomes reciprocal rescue
counterexamples_checked: high-performing compressed creature films can contain visible AI artifacts; polish alone does not explain performance
giant scale alone is insufficient unless tied to care, vulnerability, or rescue
sparse dialogue is a format choice, not permission for thin causality

packaging.thumbnail_single_read: Noor in occupational costume fleeing or standing before a barnacle-armored giant crab that hunts through tidal channels, with the stranded ferry hull and the lighthouse foghorn/lens mechanism and scale contrast instantly visible
packaging.curiosity_gap: how can a lighthouse radio operator survive a creature that owns the terrain?
packaging.visual_before_after: wrecked vehicle/station becomes the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home; bent brass foghorn valve key changes from routine tool into rescue mechanism
packaging.title_thumbnail_mismatch_risk: generic monster packaging would hide the stronger occupational-care-rescue mechanism

evidence_boundaries: Inspired by mechanism-level evidence in compressed creature-survival research; characters, species mix, vehicle, object, and rescue chain are original.
No CTR, retention, or traffic causality is claimed from public video metadata.

meaning_carrier.opening_meaning: the key is a maintenance tool Noor uses as routine maintenance before the wreck
meaning_carrier.closing_reversal: the same key opens the foghorn line that drives the crab into the tide gate and frees trapped passengers
meaning_carrier.final_sequence_use: the object operates the final light/sound/trap mechanism before the rescued group reaches the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home

relational_contract.power_asymmetry: predator-controlled terrain versus an injured professional with only knowledge, tools, and attention to vulnerable life
relational_contract.safety_or_kindness_before_power: Noor frees or protects an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire before knowing it can guide, prove, or save anyone
relational_contract.costly_protagonist_action: she turns back toward the predator territory to free captives and an ancient leatherback turtle carrying moss and shell scars instead of escaping alone
relational_contract.consent_or_personhood_repair: the allied creature is never commanded as a weapon; it chooses contact or return freely, and survivors repair their earlier dismissal of the animal
relational_contract.payoff_image: the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home; the turtle returns to open water with the seabird chick safe on its mossy shell
